formation.title: The Act of Union
formation.text:
The Acts of Union have joined the Kingdoms of England and Scotland into a single sovereign state, Great Britain. The Scottish Parliament and English Parliament are dissolved, replaced by the Parliament of Great Britain at Westminster. This is no mere conquest; it is a negotiated union, born of shared Protestant faith, economic necessity, and the hard lessons of a century of civil wars.

The question now is what manner of nation this united Britain shall become. The combined Royal Navy already rivals any fleet afloat, and the chartered trading companies reach from the Spice Islands to the Americas. But within these islands lie coal seams, iron deposits, and a population of inventors, artisans, and entrepreneurs whose energies, properly harnessed, could transform the very nature of production itself.

What shall define this new Britain?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

modifiers.name: Rule Britannia
modifiers.text: The Act of Union has forged a maritime superpower. With the combined fleets of England and Scotland, and the wealth of the world's oceans beckoning, Britain shall command the seas, protect its trade routes, and project power to every corner of the globe.

options.text: We shall be the forge of nations.

modifiers.name: Workshop of the World
modifiers.text: The union of England and Scotland creates not merely a political entity but an economic engine. With abundant natural resources, growing institutions of learning, and a culture of practical innovation, Britain shall become the workshop that supplies the world.

advances.name: Staple Ports
advances.text: The wool staple system channels English trade through designated ports, establishing regulated markets that concentrate commercial activity and generate reliable customs revenue.

advances.name: Admiralty Courts
advances.text: Specialized courts of admiralty jurisdiction settle maritime disputes, enforce prize law, and provide the legal framework for an expanding naval establishment.

advances.name: Trinity House
advances.text: In 1514 Henry VIII granted a charter to the Guild of the Holy Trinity at Deptford Strond, a fraternity of shipmen who complained that unskilled young men were piloting ships on the Thames. The guild licenses every pilot on the river and will in time keep the buoys, beacons and lighthouses of the whole coast.

advances.name: New Model Army
advances.text: Oliver Cromwell's revolutionary innovation: a professional standing army organized by merit rather than social rank, trained to strict discipline, and loyal to the cause rather than to individual commanders.

advances.name: Chartered Companies
advances.text: Royal charters grant joint-stock companies monopoly trading rights in distant regions, combining private capital with public purpose to extend British commercial reach across the globe.

advances.name: Race-Built Galleons
advances.text: Sir John Hawkins' revolutionary ship design: lower in the water, longer in proportion to beam, and faster than the towering Spanish galleons they were built to fight.

advances.name: English Dragoons
advances.text: Mounted infantry who ride to battle but fight on foot, combining the strategic mobility of cavalry with the firepower of musketeers.

advances.name: Royal Dockyards
advances.text: The great naval dockyards at Chatham, Portsmouth, and Deptford form the industrial backbone of the Royal Navy, capable of building, fitting, and repairing warships on an unprecedented scale.

advances.name: Sloop Warfare
advances.text: Small, fast sloops-of-war patrol the coastlines and trade routes, hunting pirates, escorting convoys, and maintaining British naval presence in waters too shallow or too remote for ships of the line.

advances.name: Bank of England
advances.text: The establishment of a national bank in 1694 revolutionizes government finance, providing reliable credit, stabilizing currency, and giving Britain a financial advantage that its rivals cannot match.

event.title: The Bank of England
event.text:
In 1694, William Paterson persuaded Parliament to charter a novel institution: a national bank that would lend money to the government at interest, funded by public subscription. The Bank of England has proven revolutionary. By providing the Crown with reliable credit at reasonable rates, it has freed Britain from dependence on foreign bankers and enabled the sustained funding of both war and commerce.

The Bank's notes circulate alongside coin, and its capacity to manage the national debt gives Britain a financial resilience its rivals can only envy. But how shall this institution best serve the nation? Sound monetary policy would stabilize prices and reward thrift. Alternatively, generous credit could fuel merchant ventures and construction projects across the realm.

options.text: Sound money is the foundation of lasting prosperity.

modifiers.name: Sound Money
modifiers.text: The Bank of England pursues a policy of monetary stability, maintaining the value of the pound sterling and providing reliable credit to the Crown at favorable rates.

options.text: Credit is the lifeblood of commerce.

modifiers.name: Mercantile Credit
modifiers.text: The Bank of England extends generous credit to merchants and builders alike, fueling a boom in commercial ventures and construction projects across the realm.

advances.name: Highland Regiments
advances.text: The fierce warrior traditions of the Scottish Highlands are harnessed for imperial service, as clan warriors are organized into disciplined regiments that combine Highland ferocity with British drill.

event.title: The Highland Regiments
event.text:
The pacification of the Scottish Highlands after the Jacobite risings presented Britain with both a challenge and an opportunity. The fierce warrior tradition of the Highland clans (the devastating charge with broadsword and targe, the endurance bred by mountain life) could be turned from a source of rebellion into a pillar of imperial strength.

The formation of Independent Highland Companies, later merged into the Black Watch and other regiments, channels this martial spirit into service of the Crown. Highland soldiers have already proven themselves from Fontenoy to Fort Ticonderoga, their courage and ferocity earning respect even from their enemies.

Shall we focus on integrating these proud people fully into British society, or preserve their distinct martial tradition as a weapon of empire?

options.text: Welcome them as equal subjects of the Crown.

modifiers.name: Highland Integration
modifiers.text: The Highland clans are welcomed as equal subjects of the Crown, their culture respected and their people integrated into the broader fabric of British society.

options.text: Let the Highland charge terrify our enemies.

modifiers.name: Highland Martial Tradition
modifiers.text: The fierce warrior traditions of the Scottish Highlands are preserved and celebrated, channeled into elite regiments that terrify Britain's enemies on battlefields across the globe.

advances.name: East India Trade
advances.text: The East India Company's armed merchantmen, the East Indiamen, ply the route to India and beyond, combining formidable naval capability with vast cargo capacity.

event.title: The East India Company
event.text:
What began as a modest joint-stock venture to trade in Eastern spices has become the most powerful commercial enterprise the world has ever seen. The East India Company now maintains its own armies, governs vast territories, and conducts diplomacy with sovereign rulers from the Mughal Emperor to the Sultan of Sulu.

From the warehouses of Surat to the counting houses of Calcutta, Company agents trade in cotton, silk, indigo, tea, and opium. The revenues flowing back to London fuel investment, feed the Treasury through customs duties, and make fortunes for shareholders. The East Indiaman, those great armed merchantmen that ply the route to India, have become the commercial backbone of the British Empire.

options.text: Trade is the sinew of empire.

advances.name: Royal Marines
advances.text: The Duke of York and Albany's Maritime Regiment of Foot, established in 1664, creates a permanent corps of soldiers trained for shipboard combat, boarding actions, and amphibious operations.

advances.name: Turnpike Trusts
advances.text: Private turnpike trusts charge tolls to maintain and improve roads, creating a network of reliable all-weather routes that dramatically reduce journey times and transport costs across Britain.

advances.name: British Frigate Design
advances.text: The fifth-rate frigate becomes the Royal Navy's most versatile warship: fast enough to scout for the battle fleet, powerful enough to take on enemy merchantmen, and seaworthy enough to operate independently across vast oceans.

advances.name: First Rate Ships
advances.text: The first-rate ship of the line, mounting a hundred guns or more across three decks, represents the ultimate expression of wooden warship construction and naval industrial might.

event.title: First Rates of the Line
event.text:
The first-rate ship of the line represents the pinnacle of wooden warship construction. Mounting a hundred guns or more across three decks, these floating fortresses can deliver devastating broadsides that can reduce any opposition to splinters. The Victory, the Royal Sovereign, the Britannia, their very names speak of naval supremacy.

Building and maintaining such vessels requires prodigious resources: thousands of oak trees for the hull, miles of rope and canvas, tons of iron for fittings and guns, and crews numbering eight hundred men or more. Only a nation with Britain's dockyards, its timber reserves, its trained seamen, and its financial institutions can sustain a fleet of such leviathans. They are as much a statement of industrial and organizational capacity as of naval ambition.

advances.name: Horse Guards
advances.text: The Household Cavalry, the Life Guards and Royal Horse Guards, serve as the sovereign's personal mounted bodyguard and as elite heavy cavalry on the battlefield.

advances.name: Charity Schools
advances.text: The Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge establishes charity schools across Britain, providing basic education to the children of the poor and laying the foundations of a literate workforce.

advances.name: Coal and Iron
advances.text: Britain's abundant coal seams and iron deposits, combined with innovations in smelting and metalworking, create the raw material base for an industrial transformation that will reshape the world.

destiny.name: The British Destiny
destiny.text: Great Britain stands united. The question that defines its future, whether it shall command the seas or forge a new world through industry, demands an answer. The destiny of these islands, and of the world they will shape, begins here.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The British Destiny
event.text:
Great Britain is forged. England and Scotland are no longer rivals but partners in a union of extraordinary potential. The combined resources of these islands (the dockyards of the Thames, the coal seams of the Midlands, the hardy seamen of Cornwall and the Highlands) create a nation of unmatched versatility.

But potential alone does not make greatness. The path Britain chooses will determine whether it becomes the master of the world's oceans or the workshop that reshapes civilization itself. Both roads lead to supremacy, but they demand different sacrifices and different virtues.

destiny.name: Command the Narrow Seas
destiny.text: Britain's maritime destiny begins at home. Subdue Ulster and hold Derry, where the North Channel is narrowest, to unite the archipelago, seize Calais to dominate the English Channel, and build a force worthy of a naval power. Only then can the Royal Navy project strength beyond these waters.

conditions.text: Chose Rule Britannia
Own Derry, or a subject owns it
Own Calais, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 30

event.title: Command of the Narrow Seas
event.text:
The English Channel and the Irish Sea are now British waters in truth, not merely in aspiration. With Ulster subdued, Derry walled and Calais in British hands, no fleet can threaten these islands, and no merchant vessel can pass without British leave.

The Narrow Seas are the gateway to the wider world. From this position of unassailable home defense, Britain can now project its naval power outward, to the Caribbean, to the Mediterranean, to the distant waters of the Indian Ocean.

destiny.name: Caribbean Station
destiny.text: The sugar islands of the Caribbean and the strategic bastion of Bermuda will anchor British naval power in the New World. Seize Havana from Spain, fortify the Atlantic and bring West Indian sugar into British markets: it is the trade that pays for the squadrons.

conditions.text: Own Habana, or a subject owns it
Own Bermuda, or a subject owns it
A market the country is in

children.text: Sugar is produced in the market
Sugar is traded in the market

event.title: The Caribbean Station
event.text:
British warships now patrol the turquoise waters of the Caribbean, and the Union Jack flies over Havana and Bermuda. The sugar islands produce fabulous wealth, the strategic harbors provide anchorage for squadrons that can strike anywhere in the Americas, and the trade routes home are secured against all comers.

But what shall this Caribbean dominion ultimately serve? The plantation wealth of sugar, rum, and tobacco can fuel Britain's merchant class to unprecedented prosperity. Alternatively, the Caribbean stations can become the forward operating bases of a fleet designed to control every ocean.

options.text: Let the sugar trade flow to London.

modifiers.name: Sugar Trade
modifiers.text: The Caribbean sugar plantations generate enormous wealth, enriching Britain's merchant class and concentrating commercial power in the great trading houses, though the costs of maintaining distant garrisons strain the army's budget.

options.text: Our fleet shall command every horizon.

modifiers.name: Colonial Fleet
modifiers.text: Purpose-built squadrons of fast, weatherly ships patrol the Atlantic and Caribbean, projecting British naval power across the ocean and securing every trade route for the Crown.

destiny.name: Pax Britannica
destiny.text: The ultimate expression of British naval supremacy: control the world's vital chokepoints. Gibraltar commands the Mediterranean, Aden guards the Red Sea, Bombay anchors power in India, and Singapore secures the passage to the East. The stations are kept by ships that refit where they serve: build a shipyard at Bombay, where the Wadia shipwrights built ships of the line in teak.

conditions.text: Own Gibraltar, or a subject owns it
Own 'Adan, or a subject owns it
Own Thana, or a subject owns it
Own Temasek, or a subject owns it
Bombay is owned and has a Shipyard, Grand Shipyard or Naval Base

event.title: Pax Britannica
event.text:
Gibraltar. Aden. Bombay. Singapore. Four names that together spell global dominion. Britain now controls every vital chokepoint between Europe and the East, commanding the Mediterranean passage, the Red Sea route, the Indian Ocean, and the Straits of Malacca.

No fleet can move, no merchant can trade, no empire can project power without British permission. This is the Pax Britannica, peace enforced by the unmatched power of the Royal Navy. But how shall this unprecedented supremacy be wielded? Through the direct application of force, bending rivals to British will? Or through the patient construction of an imperial system, binding subject peoples into a federation that serves London?

modifiers.name: Gunboat Diplomacy
modifiers.text: A British warship in the harbor speaks louder than any ambassador. The Royal Navy enforces treaties, opens markets, and settles disputes with the implicit threat of devastating firepower.

options.text: We shall bind the empire together.

modifiers.name: Imperial Federation
modifiers.text: The far-flung territories of the British Empire are bound together by shared institutions, common law, and the invisible threads of trade and governance, though such vast dominion breeds a dangerous complacency.

destiny.name: The United Kingdom
destiny.text: Before Britain can reshape the world, it must first consolidate the home islands. Bring Ireland into the union by ruling Dublin directly and building it into the second city of the kingdoms, foster internal stability, and ensure coal, the fuel of the coming age, flows through British markets.

event.title: The United Kingdom
event.text:
The Act of Union with Ireland completes the consolidation of the British Isles into a single political entity, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland. Dublin is ruled from Westminster and has grown into the second city of the kingdoms. With internal stability secured and the coal that will power a revolution flowing freely through British markets, the foundations of economic supremacy are laid.

The home islands are no longer a collection of feuding kingdoms but a unified economic space of extraordinary productive potential. What was once a patchwork of regional economies is becoming a single, integrated market, the largest and most sophisticated in Europe.

options.text: One kingdom, one market, one destiny.

destiny.name: The City of London
destiny.text: The square mile of the City of London shall become the financial capital of the world. Amass the wealth of a great power, raise a stock exchange in London where the brokers of Change Alley trade the nation's debt, and build London up to half again what it was.

conditions.text: Gold at least 2000
London is owned and has a Stock Exchange
London is owned and has at least 56 development

event.title: The City of London
event.text:
The City of London, that ancient square mile within the old Roman walls, has become the undisputed financial capital of the world. The Bank of England sets interest rates that ripple across continents, Lloyd's insures every ship afloat, and the Royal Exchange sets commodity prices for goods from every corner of the globe.

This concentration of financial power gives Britain leverage that armies alone cannot provide. But the City's influence can be directed in different ways. Shall it serve as a stock exchange, directing capital into productive ventures and reducing the cost of construction across the realm? Or shall it develop as an insurance and intelligence market, where the information flowing through Lloyd's and the counting houses gives Britain unmatched diplomatic advantage?

modifiers.name: Stock Exchange
modifiers.text: The London Stock Exchange channels private capital into productive investment, reducing the cost of construction and strengthening the Crown's financial position through a culture of innovation and speculation.

options.text: Information is the true currency of power.

modifiers.name: Insurance Market
modifiers.text: Lloyd's of London and the City's intelligence networks provide Britain with unmatched knowledge of global affairs, improving diplomatic relations and enabling the free flow of trade across open markets.

destiny.name: The Industrial Revolution
destiny.text: From the cotton mills of Manchester to the forges of Birmingham, Britain shall pioneer the age of machines. Build turnpike roads in four places to carry their coal, cotton and iron, and build both towns up to twice what they were, into manufacturing cities whose productive capacity dwarfs all rivals.

conditions.text: Has a Turnpike Road in at least 4 locations
Manchester is owned and has at least 34 development
Birmingham is owned and has at least 44 development

event.title: The Industrial Revolution
event.text:
The world will never be the same. In the cotton mills of Manchester and the iron foundries of Birmingham, a revolution is underway that will transform human civilization more profoundly than any conquest. Steam engines pump water from mines, drive looms that produce cloth a hundred times faster than hand weavers, and power bellows that smelt iron in quantities previously unimaginable.

Britain stands at the epicenter of this transformation. But what shall the Industrial Revolution ultimately mean for British society? The raw productive power of steam can be channeled into military and logistical supremacy, enabling faster mobilization and movement of armies. Or the social upheaval of industrialization can be harnessed through parliamentary reform, extending the franchise, abolishing old injustices, and building a more stable society.

modifiers.name: Steam Power
modifiers.text: The steam engine transforms not only industry but warfare. Faster recruitment, improved logistics, and the concentration of productive capacity in Britain's great cities give the nation a decisive military-industrial advantage.

modifiers.name: The Reform Acts
modifiers.text: Parliamentary reform extends the franchise, abolishes rotten boroughs, and addresses the social upheavals of industrialization. A more representative government commands greater loyalty and reduces the appeal of separatism and revolution.

units.name: Race-Built Galleon
units.text: A revolutionary English warship design with a lower profile, longer hull, and superior sailing qualities compared to the towering galleons of rival navies.

units.name: Sloop-of-War
units.text: A small, fast patrol vessel designed for convoy escort, anti-piracy operations, and coastal patrol duties.

units.name: East Indiaman
units.text: A heavily-built armed merchantman of the East India Company, designed for the long and dangerous voyage to India and the Far East.

units.name: British Frigate
units.text: The versatile fifth-rate warship of the Royal Navy, fast enough to scout and powerful enough to fight independently across the world's oceans.

units.name: First Rate
units.text: The ultimate expression of the wooden warship: a three-decked, hundred-gun floating fortress capable of devastating broadsides.

units.name: New Model Pikemen
units.text: Disciplined professional soldiers of the New Model Army tradition, trained to stand firm under fire and push pike with mechanical precision.

units.name: English Dragoons
units.text: Mounted infantry who ride to battle but dismount to fight, combining strategic mobility with firepower.

units.name: Royal Marines
units.text: Professional soldiers trained for shipboard combat, boarding actions, and amphibious landings. The sea soldiers of the Crown.

units.name: Horse Guards
units.text: The elite Household Cavalry of the British sovereign, combining ceremonial splendor with devastating battlefield capability.

buildings.name: Royal Dockyard
buildings.text: A major naval shipbuilding and repair facility, capable of constructing warships of all rates and maintaining the fleet in fighting condition.

buildings.name: Trading Factory
buildings.text: A commercial warehouse and trading post operated by chartered merchants, concentrating trade activity and extending British commercial networks.

buildings.name: Turnpike Road
buildings.text: A toll road maintained by a private trust, providing reliable all-weather transport that connects markets and reduces journey times.

buildings.name: Charity School
buildings.text: A school funded by charitable subscription to educate the children of the poor, spreading literacy and useful knowledge among the laboring classes.

buildings.name: Admiralty Office
buildings.text: A regional office of naval administration, coordinating fleet operations, managing sailor recruitment, and maintaining maritime records.

buildings.name: Trinity House
buildings.text: A house of the pilots' guild in a harbour town. Its brethren examine and license pilots, lay buoys on the shoals, and keep the beacons burning that bring ships in after dark.

buildings.name: Royal Arsenal
buildings.text: A vast military-industrial complex combining shipbuilding, ordnance production, and garrison facilities, capable of equipping and maintaining both naval and land forces on a scale that no rival can match.

buildings.name: Industrial Works
buildings.text: A mechanized manufacturing facility powered by steam and coal, producing goods at a speed and scale that transforms the local economy and draws workers from across the region.

list.name: Justices of the Peace
list.text: Formalised by the Justices of the Peace Act of 1361, the lay magistrates of the shires became the mainstay of Tudor local government. Drawn from the landed gentry, the JPs tried felonies at quarter sessions, administered the poor laws, mustered the militia, and effectively governed the English counties until the reformed county councils of the 19th century. Their authority is the Crown's, but their interests are unmistakably those of the squirearchy.

list.name: Court of Star Chamber
list.text: Sitting in the star-painted chamber at the Palace of Westminster from Henry VII's Star Chamber Act of 1487 until its abolition by the Long Parliament in 1641, this prerogative court of the King's Council bypassed common-law juries to bring overmighty subjects to heel. Under Cardinal Wolsey's chancellorship the Star Chamber became formidable; under the early Stuarts it became the byword for royal absolutism, and the price its closure exacted from the Crown was paid in 1649.

list.name: The Exchequer
list.text: Constituted by Henry I in the early 12th century and named for the chequered cloth on which sheriffs' accounts were reckoned, the Exchequer audited every receipt and disbursement of the Crown twice a year. The Pipe Rolls produced by its barons anchored English fiscal administration for seven centuries, until the department's formal end with the Exchequer and Audit Departments Act of 1833 left only the Bank of England's Exchequer account behind.

list.name: The Royal Mint
list.text: Henry II's Tealby coinage of 1158 set the sterling silver standard at 92.5 percent fineness, a benchmark held, with notorious debasements, until 1920. Housed within the Tower of London under the King's Assay Master, the Mint's coinage was annually verified by the Trial of the Pyx, the oldest continuous quality-assurance process in the realm. Sound coin underwrites both the merchant's confidence in long-distance trade and the Crown's reputation for honest dealing.

list.name: Navy Board
list.text: Established by letters patent of Henry VIII on 24 April 1546 as the Council of the Marine, the Navy Board made the Royal Navy a permanent institution rather than a fleet hired campaign by campaign. The Treasurer, Surveyor, Comptroller, and Clerk of the Navy administered the dockyards at Deptford, Woolwich, and Portsmouth and managed every contract for timber, cordage, and gunfounding. From 1628 it answered to the Board of Admiralty, but its dockyard expertise outlasted every reorganisation.

list.name: Bank of England
list.text: Chartered on 27 July 1694 under the Tonnage Act on Charles Montagu's plan, the Governor and Company of the Bank of England lent GBP 1.2 million to William III's war government in exchange for note-issue privileges and the management of the consolidated debt. By converting short-term war borrowing into perpetual annuities at predictable rates, the Bank gave Britain the sustained credit on which the fiscal-military state and the long 18th-century wars with France were built.

conditions.text: Any of

list.name: Parliament of Westminster
list.text: The 1707 Acts of Union dissolved the Edinburgh and English parliaments and convened a single Parliament of Great Britain at Westminster, with Scottish representative peers in the Lords and 45 Scottish members in the Commons. Its legislative supremacy after 1689 made it the indispensable guarantor of the fiscal-military state: parliamentary taxes secured public credit and made the Bank of England's charter sound. The price was a permanent dilution of the royal prerogative.
